extracted.intended_audience: International doctoral candidates and early postdoctoral researchers applying for DAAD Research Grants in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for applying to DAAD Research Grants in Germany for doctoral students and early postdocs, including eligibility, required documents, funding details, and selection criteria used by the independent selection committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the programme
rubrics_metrics.description: The research grant offers the opportunity to realise a research project in Germany. The programme supports research stays during a doctorate or in the early postdoc phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project must be carried out at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany and be carried out in agreement with a scientific supervisor in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — doctoral students
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you are doing your doctorate at a university or research institution outside Germany and the start of your doctorate should not be more than 3 years ago at the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot apply if you are doing your entire doctorate at a German university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — postdocs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you have already completed your doctorate (post-doc, up to 4 years after completing your doctorate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For postdocs the rule is: you should not have completed your doctorate more than 4 years before the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application cannot be considered if you have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must check residency duration carefully; if residence >15 months, application is ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific additional regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, further regulations apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in these fields must consult the linked additional regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: What can be funded (host institution and supervisor requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A research project at a state or state-recognised university or a non-university research institute in Germany, which is being carried out in agreement with a scientific supervisor in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirmation from the academic host in Germany must refer to your project and guarantee that the host institute will provide a workplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of funding — doctoral students
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is provided for a period of 2 to 12 months for doctoral students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not possible to divide the funding up within the funding period. The funding must begin in 2026. The funding period will be determined by the selection committee during the selection process, taking your work schedule into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of funding — postdocs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is provided for a period of 2 to 6 months for postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same constraints: cannot divide periods, must begin in 2026, scholarship cannot be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding non-extendable and not divisible
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholarship cannot be extended and it is not possible to divide the funding up within the funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned research work in different countries outside Germany is not eligible for funding; plan a continuous stay in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship amount and core benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly scholarship payments of 1.400 euros and payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See important information for scholarship applicants (section F, point 4) for details on insurance coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and research allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel allowance and for a funding period of more than six months: research allowance of 460 euros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check exact entitlement rules; phrasing indicates different allowances may apply depending on duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional benefits after start of funding (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances, additional benefits may be applied for after the start of funding, e.g., monthly rent subsidy (only for funding >6 months), monthly allowance for accompanying family members (only for funding >6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should read important scholarship information, section F, for precise conditions and application procedures for these benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for disability or chronic illness
rubrics_metrics.description: On application, a subsidy may be provided for justified additional costs incurred abroad that are necessary to realise the project in Germany and that are not covered by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether and to what extent a subsidy will be paid will be reviewed and determined on an individual basis (see important information, section F, point 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Mobility Top Up / carbon offset reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for Green Mobility Top Up (subsidy for climate-friendly travel) or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be available according to DAAD rules; applicants should consult the detailed scholarship info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language training benefits for funding >6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: For funding periods of more than six months DAAD may pay course fees for an online language course after receipt of the Scholarship Award Letter and possibly fund German language course in Germany before the start of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAAD decides whether to fund participation and for how long depending on German language skills and project; allowance for personally chosen German language course during scholarship period; reimbursement of TestDaF or DSH test fee (either in home country after award or in Germany during funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party benefits offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits from third parties are partially credited towards the DAAD scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See important scholarship information section F, point 6 for rules on how third-party funding affects DAAD payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent selection committee consisting of specialist scientists reviews the applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is competitive and handled by subject specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — Academic Qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic achievements (grade point average, development of grades); academic progress; knowledge of the language(s) of instruction or working language(s); if applicable, scholarly achievements after graduation (e.g. publications, lectures, conference papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide records (certificates, transcripts) and evidence of post-graduation scholarly work where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — Quality of research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of research proposal and preparation (originality, topicality and relevance of the project, choice of host institution and first contacts); feasibility and consistency of study plan and schedule; incorporation of project within the overall doctorate (in terms of content and time), if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal should be prepared and formulated by the applicant and discussed with the academic adviser in Germany. Follow proposal formatting and length guidance (max. 10 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — Potential of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Career prospects: significance of the research project and stay in Germany for further academic, professional and personal development; motivation: academic and personal reasons for wanting to visit Germany, German language skills (if different from working language); non-study-related activities: non-study-related knowledge and skills, civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter of motivation (1–2 pages) should address what the applicant hopes to gain personally, professionally and for their career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection committee gives due consideration to equal opportunities; applicants can provide relevant information in the application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant data may be provided in the application form per instructions in the important scholarship information (section E, point 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application validity and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application is only valid if you submit all the required documents to the DAAD portal by the application deadline. Incomplete applications cannot be considered. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their applications are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portal closes at 24.00 hrs. (CET or CEST) on the last application day. If possible, do not submit on the final date to avoid technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal access and technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The access to the DAAD portal opens at least 6 weeks before the application deadline. The usage of the application portal is possible only to a limited extent with mobile devices — use a desktop computer. Only PDF files can be uploaded to the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare documents as PDFs, translate documents if necessary, and be aware the portal only appears while the current application period is running.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document format, translation and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates, proof of credits, certifications and translations may be scanned in non-certified form and uploaded to the DAAD portal. The DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies of the documents. If documents are submitted in your national language, include German or English translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload original-language document and translation together; DAAD may later require certified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under the appropriate portal field; concise tabular CV expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — list of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: List of your published publications (max. 10 pages); mandatory for postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdocs must include publication list; doctoral candidates include if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — letter of motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of motivation, 1 - 2 pages: statement about the academic and personal reasons for the planned research project in Germany, taking account of the following question: What do you hope to gain from your project in Germany (personally, professionally, for your career)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload the letter under 'study project/motivation' in the DAAD portal; address both academic and personal motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal (max. 10 pages in total), prepared and formulated by yourself; a proposal is an extensive and detailed description of the research project which has been discussed with the academic adviser in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under 'research project' in the DAAD portal. See important scholarship information (section B, point 2) for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — time schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Time schedule of planned research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a feasible timeline; selection committee assesses feasibility and consistency with study plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — proof of doctoral enrolment/admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of admission to doctoral studies/enrolment for doctoral studies (for doctoral students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under 'proof of admission' in the portal. If the most recent degree certificate is not yet available, it must be submitted before the start of the scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — confirmation from academic host
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation from the academic host in Germany; the confirmation must refer to your project and guarantee that the host institute in Germany will provide you with a workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under 'acceptance of host institution' in the DAAD portal. See important scholarship information (section C, point 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — declaration on research safety/ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration from the scientific supervisor in Germany on safety-relevant and ethical aspects of the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload the document under 'Scientific ethics/research safety' in the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — university degree certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: University degree certificates (e.g. Bachelor's, Master's, doctorate) stating your final grade(s); if you do not have your most recent degree certificate (doctoral candidates: Master's; postdocs: doctorate) at the time of application, you must submit it before the start of your scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload under 'university degree certificates' in the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents — supporting letter of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: One recent supporting letter of recommendation (on a DAAD-form) from a university teacher (for doctoral students, from the supervisor of your doctoral thesis) which provides information about your qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate the recommendation form in the DAAD Portal during the application period, send to referee to complete, then upload it under 'Letter of Recommendation'. Follow portal instructions for requesting and uploading the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional additional documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Other documents you think might be of relevance to your application (e.g. certificates of employment, proof of extracurricular engagement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload as optional attachments; label clearly and include translations if not in German or English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After registering on the DAAD portal, complete the online application in full and upload all application documents in the section 'Attachments'. The access to the DAAD portal opens at least 6 weeks before the application deadline and only appears while the current application period is running.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portal closes at 24.00 hrs (CET or CEST) on last application day. Prepare and upload PDFs in advance; allow for processing time if you need technical support (portal@daad.de or hotline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical support and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any technical questions or problems your local information and advice centres could not help you with, contact portal@daad.de or call the technical portal hotline on weekdays from 9-12 and 14-16 (CET/CEST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider possible processing times when planning your application; do not wait until the final day if technical problems may arise.
